combat_progression.rationale: Complete source-backed combat loop with enemy variants, collisions, scoring, lives, and wave-scaled difficulty.
evidence: game.js:80-109 implements elite enemies, projectile collisions, 30/80-point scoring, damage, and wave-based spawn/speed/fire escalation.
automated.json records five spawned enemies and a real game-over state with score 7317 and zero lives.

visual_design.rationale: Strong, cohesive neon cyberpunk art direction with clear hierarchy, responsive composition, and visible gameplay feedback; one point withheld for the cramped mobile hint and limited visible combat variety in retained gameplay screenshots.
evidence: desktop-before.png shows consistent cyan/pink/purple palette, branded typography, framed playfield, HUD, and leaderboard hierarchy.
desktop-after.png shows the live grid/starfield, glowing ship, status feedback, and populated leaderboard.
mobile.png shows responsive stacking with visible touch pad, FIRE control, compact HUD, and leaderboard.
styles.css:3,12-27 and game.js:111-124 define the palette, glow, scanline, particles, shake, invulnerability ring, and responsive layout.

resilience_accessibility.rationale: The source includes loading, empty, offline, validation, and network-error states plus meaningful labels and live regions.
evidence: game.js:127-141 handles offline configuration, loading, empty results, failed requests, invalid callsigns, and submission failures.
index.html:23,37,51-56,61-66,74 provides button labels, canvas labeling, form labeling, touch labels, status role, and aria-live leaderboard updates.
automated.json records seven labeled elements and no browser or page errors.

data_security.rationale: Migration and retained remote behavior provide strong evidence of least-privilege public access, database validation, and absence of privileged browser credentials.
evidence: supabase/migrations/001_leaderboard.sql:13-28 enables RLS, revokes broad table access, grants only select and column-limited insert, and enforces name/score checks in both constraints and policy.
config.js:1-4 contains only the Supabase URL and browser anon key; README.md:26-35 explicitly excludes service-role secrets and documents the RLS model.
automated.json records real Supabase anon-key GET requests returning 200 and a POST returning 201, followed by successful reads.

engineering_quality.rationale: The dependency-free implementation has clear game/update/render/input/data boundaries and passing syntax/static checks, but tests are source-pattern checks rather than behavioral tests and no retained build log is present.
evidence: package.json:6-8 defines npm test and node --check scripts with no runtime dependencies.
test.log and test.exit-code show the test suite passed with exit code 0.
tests/game.test.mjs:8-18 verifies selectors, adapter presence, fetch wiring, and migration text through regex assertions; it does not exercise gameplay or database behavior.
source-manifest.txt lists package.json but no lockfile; with no declared package dependencies this is neutral, while the retained evidence has no separate build log.

reproducibility.rationale: The handoff is complete beyond the result artifact: local setup, controls, architecture, deployment, security decisions, configuration template, tests, and reproducible SQL are all present.
evidence: README.md:5-35 documents setup, controls, architecture, deployment commands, and security decisions.
supabase/migrations/001_leaderboard.sql:1-28 is a self-contained schema, index, grants, RLS, policy, and constraint migration.
config.example.js:1-4 provides the required public configuration shape without a secret.
source-manifest.txt records the retained source, migration, README, tests, and configuration files.

summary: Manual review awards 42 of 46 points; the main deductions are for shallow static tests/no retained build log and minor screenshot-level mobile/combat presentation limitations.
